## Preparing Grant is boring

1. Nobody loves writing grant applications

2. There is no shortcut to the boring part


## A grant mindset 

1. look actively for grant

2. ask/imitate colleagues

## You need to spend LOT of time in writing the grant

1. If you think it is excellent it will be very good
  
2. if you think it is very good it will be sufficient

## Apply to the right grant

1. Assess probability of winning and time required to write the grant, before applying

2. only apply when you have a reasonable probability of winning


    
## Prepare your grant project (coarsely) before 
   
1. don’t expect the call to sketch the idea
   
## Finds your (potential) partner before

1. you should pre-alert partner and secure them before

## Spend time to study the documents of the application

1. it is not just about the idea! (everyone loves the own ideas)

2. Check who won in previous calls (these are typically publicly available)

3. e.g. Roche, Finalizzata

## Beware of criteria and on how scoring works

3. If you just meet the prerequisites, you will start with a disadvantage
    
## Grants win grants

1. Sad but true

2. Sometimes you need to be **Be part of a winning team**, not the winner

3. Start as Co-pi (or partner)


## Think about funding agency (reviewers)

1. Don’t just write what you think it is important, write what the funding agency think is important (see all past points).

## Remember that you will have to run the project

1. Plan ahead the feasibility of the project

2. Avoid setting overly ambitious goals “just in case.” or "to impress reviewers"
